decision.trend: The trend in the research is to develop high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with improved strength and ductility. Various processing techniques such as vacuum induction melting, hot isostatic pressing, and selective laser melting have been used to produce HEAs with unique microstructures. The addition of alloying elements and the use of thermo-mechanical processes have been explored to enhance the mechanical properties of HEAs. The research has also focused on understanding the deformation mechanisms and the role of precipitates in improving the strength and ductility of HEAs.
decision.unsolved: One of the major challenges in the development of HEAs is the trade-off between strength and ductility. While some HEAs have shown improved strength, they often suffer from reduced ductility. Further research is needed to develop HEAs that can simultaneously achieve high strength and ductility.
decision.why: The next step in the research would be to use machine learning-based methods to design new HEAs with optimized compositions and microstructures. This approach could help to identify new alloying elements and processing conditions that can lead to improved strength and ductility. By using computational methods, researchers can quickly screen a large number of potential alloys and identify the most promising candidates for experimental verification.
